data.content_ref: inline:Make attack edges first-class warrant-carrying nodes: for each attack A→B add an edge-node E with E→B, and allow any argument C to attack E (C→E). Compute the grounded extension on the expanded AF. An attack only refutes B when E is accepted (every attacker of E is out), so attacking the warrant itself defeats the refutation. This preserves determinism and polynomial cost because the expansion adds one node and at most one extra edge per existing attack and the grounded fixpoint algorithm is unchanged. Committed roots remain valid if no accepted attack-edge points at them. Weakness: accepted A and accepted E both attack B, which can double-count; a merge/identity rule is needed to decide whether the original A→B still exists when E is out.
